newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Committee refutes claims that Singapore too costly.
newsitem.headline: Committee refutes claims that Singapore too costly.

text.p: Spending by Singaporeans rose by 76 percent in the five years to fiscal 1992/1993 (April-March) but actual price increases accounted for only 14 percentage points of the total, a government-appointed committee said on Friday.
The committee's findings were seen as refuting claims by opposition politicians that the cost of living in Singapore was rising too fast for its citizens to keep up.

Members of the committee said at a news conference that the remaining 62 percent rise was attributable to "other factors", particularly lifestyle changes resulting in purchases of better-quality food, clothing and household appliances.
The committee also said that between 1992 and 1995, hospital fees rose only 4.4 percent annually, public transport costs rose less than 2.0 percent, and university fees grew only 3.7 percent.
Public housing costs rose more sharply, by between 5.4 percent and 11 percent a year, they said.
"The increases are also due to an increase in wages," said committee chairman Lim Boon Heng. "The increases have not been as alarming and not as high as it is made up to be."
The committee did not say how much wages had risen.
The committee was formed in 1992 to study public concerns over the rising cost of living in Singapore.

It was reconvened in July after claims by two opposition parties, the Singapore Democratic Party and Singapore Malay National Organisation, that cost increases in recent years had been "no less than phenomenal".

The two parties had said rising costs accounted for most of the 76 percent rise in household spending during the five-year period ending in 1992/93, leading to housing, health and education moving beyond the reach of Singaporeans.
They also questioned the accuracy of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) of inflation and suggested there had been a "statistical massage of numbers" to hide a rise in costs.
But the committee said the CPI had been calculated using sound methods and in line with international standards.
